cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(Aspose_PDF_FOSS VERSION 1.0.1 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

# Python is needed only at build time, to embed the 12 Liberation
# TTF binaries into a generated `.inc` data table consumed by
# foundation::standard14_outlines. The custom command below uses
# the absolute Python interpreter path so the script runs on
# Windows where `python3.exe` is absent from python.org installs
# (Microsoft Store Python provides a `python3` shim, python.org
# does not).
find_package(Python3 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Interpreter)

# Default to Release when no build type is specified. Without this
# CMake leaves CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE empty and uses -O0 -g, which makes
# the rasterizer + TrueType parser ~10x slower than they need to
# be (concretely: full test suite goes from ~2s in Release to
# ~12s in unoptimized). Pass `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` explicitly
# when stepping through code in a debugger.
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING
      "Default build type; override with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug" FORCE)
endif()

include(FetchContent)

FetchContent_Declare(
  googletest
  URL      https://github.com/google/googletest/archive/refs/tags/v1.14.0.tar.gz
  URL_HASH SHA256=8ad598c73ad796e0d8280b082cebd82a630d73e73cd3c70057938a6501bba5d7
)
# Test-only dependency: keep GoogleTest out of `cmake --install` so the
# installed tree / release archives contain only this library.
set(INSTALL_GTEST OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(googletest)

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Library
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Source list — explicit, NOT a recursive glob.
#
# The library compiles only the public-API bodies plus the foundation
# primitives those bodies transitively need. Foundation primitives that
# exist on disk for capabilities not yet shipped (image decoding, font
# rasterisation, etc.) are NOT compiled — they'd pull additional system
# dependencies (libtiff, ...) for no current caller.
#
# Add foundation primitives here as their public-API consumers land.

set(ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_SOURCES

  src/public/document.cpp

  src/internal/binarize_bradley.cpp
)

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Standard14 outlines bundle generator. The 12 Liberation TTF binaries
# under src/foundation/standard14_outlines/fonts/ are embedded into
# the static lib via a build-time-generated .inc file (avoids
# committing a 27 MB constexpr-array source to git). Re-generates
# whenever any TTF or the generator script changes.
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set(STANDARD14_OUTLINES_GENERATOR
  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/internal/standard14_outlines.fonts/standard14_outlines.py")
set(STANDARD14_OUTLINES_FONTS_DIR
  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/internal/standard14_outlines.fonts")
set(STANDARD14_OUTLINES_INC
  "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/standard14_outlines_bundle.inc")
file(GLOB STANDARD14_OUTLINES_TTFS
  CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
  "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_FONTS_DIR}/*.ttf")
add_custom_command(
  OUTPUT "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_INC}"
  COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}" "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_GENERATOR}"
          "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_INC}"
  DEPENDS "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_GENERATOR}"
          ${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_TTFS}
  COMMENT "Generating standard14_outlines_bundle.inc from Liberation TTFs"
  VERBATIM
)
add_custom_target(standard14_outlines_inc
  DEPENDS "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_INC}")
set_source_files_properties(
  src/internal/standard14_outlines.cpp
  PROPERTIES OBJECT_DEPENDS "${STANDARD14_OUTLINES_INC}")

add_library(aspose_pdf_foss STATIC ${ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_SOURCES})
# PUBLIC so consumers (in-tree or via find_package) also compile as C++20:
# the public headers use std::span and other C++20 library features.
target_compile_features(aspose_pdf_foss PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
target_include_directories(aspose_pdf_foss
  PUBLIC
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
    $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
  PRIVATE
    # Internal foundation headers live in a single tree —
    # ``#include "lexer.hpp"`` etc. resolve via this PRIVATE flag.
    # PRIVATE because these are implementation headers, not part of
    # the lib's public API surface.
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/include/internal
    # .inc helper data files for a few primitives are siblings of
    # their .cpp under src/internal/; they're #include'd into the
    # body's anonymous namespace at compile time.
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/internal
    # Generated standard14_outlines_bundle.inc lands in the build dir.
    ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
)

# MSVC interprets source bytes as the system code page (CP-1252
# on en-US Windows, CP-936/932 on Asian locales) unless told
# otherwise. Many of our sources contain UTF-8 multibyte chars in
# both comments and string literals (em dashes, ≥, →, π, …) — see
# `error message strings throughout src/internal/`. /utf-8 forces
# both source and execution charset to UTF-8 so MSVC doesn't emit
# C4819 warnings or produce mojibake error messages at runtime.
# GCC / Clang accept UTF-8 by default and need no equivalent flag.
target_compile_options(aspose_pdf_foss PRIVATE
  $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:/utf-8 /MP>
)

# C4250 ("inherits ... via dominance") fires for every facade class:
# IFacade is a virtual base reached through both Facade and
# ISaveableFacade, and Facade's BindPdf/Close overrides win by
# dominance. That is the intended resolution, so the warning is noise. PUBLIC so tests, examples and downstream consumers that
# include the public headers don't see it either.
target_compile_options(aspose_pdf_foss PUBLIC
  $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:/wd4250>
)

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Tests
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This aggregator builds the gtest-style unit-test suite. It picks
# up only files matching the gtest naming convention
# (`*_smoke_test.cpp` and `*.cc`); any standalone int-main()
# programs under tests/internal/ are excluded so they don't collide
# with gtest_main.
enable_testing()
file(GLOB_RECURSE ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*_smoke_test.cpp"
  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*.cc"
)
list(FILTER ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX
     "/tests/internal/")
if(NOT ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES)
  file(WRITE "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_stub_test.cpp" "int main(){return 0;}\n")
  set(ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_stub_test.cpp")
endif()

add_executable(aspose_pdf_foss_tests ${ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES})
target_link_libraries(aspose_pdf_foss_tests PRIVATE
  aspose_pdf_foss
  GTest::gtest_main
)
# Tests that exercise foundation primitives directly need access to
# their headers — single PRIVATE include path covers them all under
# the flat layout.
target_include_directories(aspose_pdf_foss_tests PRIVATE
  ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/include/internal
)
target_compile_options(aspose_pdf_foss_tests PRIVATE
  $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:/utf-8 /MP>
)

# Register the whole gtest binary as ONE ctest test. Running every
# case in a single process keeps ctest fast on all filesystems —
# notably WSL's /mnt 9p mount, where per-test gtest_discover_tests
# would re-launch (and re-page-in) the 15 MB binary hundreds of times.
# Per-test visibility is preserved via gtest's JUnit XML, which CI
# ingests (artifacts:reports:junit). To run a single case locally, use
# the binary's own filter, e.g.
#   ./aspose_pdf_foss_tests --gtest_filter=TextStateSmoke.MeasureStringHelvetica
if(ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES AND NOT ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_TEST_SOURCES STREQUAL "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_stub_test.cpp")
  add_test(
    NAME aspose_pdf_foss_tests
    COMMAND aspose_pdf_foss_tests
            --gtest_output=xml:${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/gtest-results.xml)
endif()

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Examples — standalone programs showing how to call the public API.
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
add_subdirectory(examples)

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Install + CMake package export
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Consumers of an installed tree (or a release archive) use
#   find_package(aspose_pdf_foss CONFIG REQUIRED)
#   target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
# The alias lets add_subdirectory() consumers spell it the same way.
add_library(aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss ALIAS aspose_pdf_foss)

include(GNUInstallDirs)
include(CMakePackageConfigHelpers)

set(ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_CMAKE_DIR ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/cmake/aspose_pdf_foss)

install(TARGETS aspose_pdf_foss
  EXPORT aspose_pdf_foss_targets
  LIBRARY DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
  RUNTIME DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}
)
# Public headers only — include/internal/ is implementation detail and
# no public header includes it.
install(DIRECTORY include/aspose DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR})
install(FILES include/aspose.pdf.foss.hpp DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR})

install(EXPORT aspose_pdf_foss_targets
  FILE aspose_pdf_fossTargets.cmake
  NAMESPACE aspose_pdf_foss::
  DESTINATION ${ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_CMAKE_DIR}
)
configure_package_config_file(
  cmake/aspose_pdf_fossConfig.cmake.in
  ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/aspose_pdf_fossConfig.cmake
  INSTALL_DESTINATION ${ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_CMAKE_DIR}
)
write_basic_package_version_file(
  ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/aspose_pdf_fossConfigVersion.cmake
  VERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION}
  COMPATIBILITY SameMajorVersion
)
install(FILES
  ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/aspose_pdf_fossConfig.cmake
  ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/aspose_pdf_fossConfigVersion.cmake
  DESTINATION ${ASPOSE_PDF_FOSS_CMAKE_DIR}
)

# License texts travel with the binaries: MIT for the library, and the
# OFL 1.1 for the Liberation fonts compiled into it (the OFL requires
# the license to accompany redistributed font data).
install(FILES
  LICENSE
  THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
  src/internal/standard14_outlines.fonts/OFL.txt
  src/internal/standard14_outlines.fonts/AUTHORS
  DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_DATADIR}/doc/aspose_pdf_foss
)

contributing.content:
# Contributing to Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++

Thanks for your interest in contributing! This document covers how to
build, test, and submit changes.

## Building

Requirements: a C++20 compiler (clang ≥ 16, gcc ≥ 13, or MSVC 2022 ≥
17.5), CMake ≥ 3.22, and Python 3 (used by a build step that embeds the
bundled font outlines).

```bash
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build -j
```

The static library lands at `build/libaspose_pdf_foss.a` (`.lib` on
MSVC). See [`README.md`](README.md) for the full requirements and a
quick-start tour of the API.

## Running the tests

```bash
cmake --build build
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
```

The test suite uses [GoogleTest](https://github.com/google/googletest),
which CMake fetches automatically at configure time (this needs network
access on the first configure).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `include/aspose/pdf/` | Public, consumer-facing API headers |
| `include/internal/`   | Internal foundation-primitive headers |
| `src/public/`         | Public-API implementation |
| `src/internal/`       | Foundation primitives (codecs, parsers, rasteriser, …) |
| `tests/`              | GoogleTest unit + smoke tests |
| `examples/`           | Runnable demo programs |
| `pdfs/`               | Small sample PDFs used by the examples |

Public-API code under `src/public/` calls into the foundation primitives
under `src/internal/`; the primitives never reach back into the public
API.

## Coding conventions

- Match the style of the surrounding code (indentation, naming, comment
  density). The codebase is C++20 and dependency-free at runtime — please
  keep it that way; do not introduce third-party runtime dependencies.
- Keep public headers under `include/aspose/pdf/` clean: the public
  surface mirrors the canonical Aspose.PDF API names and shapes. Public
  headers must never include anything from `include/internal/`, because
  only `include/aspose/` is installed. When you add a public header, also
  add it to the single-entry header `include/aspose.pdf.foss.hpp`.
- Add or update tests under `tests/` for any behavioural change, and make
  sure `ctest` is green before opening a pull request.

## Submitting a pull request

1. Fork the repository and create a topic branch.
2. Make your change with accompanying tests.
3. Ensure `cmake --build build` and `ctest` both pass.
4. Open a pull request describing the change and the motivation.

By submitting a contribution you agree that it is licensed under the
project's [MIT License](LICENSE).

## Releasing

Releases are built by [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)
when a `vX.Y.Z` tag is pushed (`vX.Y.Z-rc.1` and similar produce a
pre-release). The version follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).

1. **Bump the version** in `project(Aspose_PDF_FOSS VERSION X.Y.Z ...)` in
   `CMakeLists.txt`. The workflow fails if the tag and this version
   differ. If the major version changes, also update the version in
   `find_package(aspose_pdf_foss X.Y ...)` in
   `.github/package-test/CMakeLists.txt`.
2. **Update `CHANGELOG.md`.** Move the `[Unreleased]` entries into a new
   `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` section and update the compare links at the
   bottom.
3. **Write release notes** (optional). The GitHub release body is taken from
   `.github/release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md` when that file exists, and otherwise
   from the `## [X.Y.Z]` section of `CHANGELOG.md`.
4. **Dry-run the packaging** (optional). Run the *Release* workflow by hand
   on your branch (Actions → Release → Run workflow). It builds and tests
   the archives and uploads them as workflow artifacts, without creating a
   release.
5. **Commit, tag, and push:**
   ```bash
   git commit -am "Release X.Y.Z"
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ X.Y.Z"
   git push origin main vX.Y.Z
   ```
6. **Publish on GitHub.** The workflow builds and tests Linux x64 (GCC 13)
   and Windows x64 (MSVC Release + Debug), packages each `cmake --install`
   tree, and compiles and runs `.github/package-test` against every
   package. It also builds the NuGet package (see below). It then creates
   a **draft** GitHub release with the archives, the `.nupkg`, and
   `SHA256SUMS.txt` attached. Review the draft, but **do not publish it
   yet**: its `.nupkg` is unsigned.
7. **Sign and publish on nuget.org.** nuget.org requires packages under
   the reserved `Aspose.` prefix to be signed with the Aspose
   code-signing certificate, which is only available to Aspose's internal
   release pipeline. That pipeline takes the tag, downloads the `.nupkg`
   from the draft, signs and verifies it, replaces the draft's `.nupkg`
   and its `SHA256SUMS.txt` line with the signed package, and pushes the
   same bytes to nuget.org. A version pushed to nuget.org cannot be
   deleted, only unlisted.
8. **Publish on GitHub.** Press *Publish release* on the draft.

Re-running the workflow for an existing tag replaces the release's assets
and leaves its notes unchanged. nuget.org skips a version that has already
been pushed.

### NuGet package

The `Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS` package targets Visual Studio (MSBuild) C++
projects. It contains static libraries for x64, x86, and ARM64, each in
Release (`/MD`) and Debug (`/MDd`, with embedded `/Z7` debug info), plus
`build/native/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS.targets`, which wires up the include
path, the library, and C++20. The sources are in `nuget/`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `nuget/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS.nuspec` | Package metadata and layout |
| `nuget/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS.targets` | MSBuild integration shipped in `build/native/` |
| `nuget/README.md` | Readme shown on nuget.org |
| `nuget/pack.ps1` | Builds, tests, packs, and verifies the package |
| `nuget/test/PackageConsumer.vcxproj` | Visual Studio consumer used to verify the packed `.nupkg` |

To build the package locally (Visual Studio 2022+ with the x64/x86 and
ARM64 C++ build tools, CMake, and Python 3 are required):

```powershell
./nuget/pack.ps1                     # all platforms; version from CMakeLists.txt
./nuget/pack.ps1 -Platforms x64      # quicker, single platform
```

The script writes `build/nuget/out/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS.<version>.nupkg`
and verifies it by building `PackageConsumer.vcxproj` against the packed
package for every platform and configuration. It runs the result wherever
the host can; ARM64 is build-only on x64 hosts.

Packages built here are unsigned. nuget.org accepts `Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS`
only when it is signed with the Aspose code-signing certificate, so
publishing always goes through Aspose's internal release pipeline (see
*Releasing*, step 7). The pipeline needs a GitHub token with *Contents:
Read and write* on this repository to read the draft release and replace
its `.nupkg`.
